Coded claim 4 text (original paper): “In Table 2, we assess only the relative weight
placed on sociotropic and security evaluations, which are two areas where presidents bear
some responsibility for performance in the eyes of voters…Likewise, citizens’ perceptions
of the government’s efforts to combat insecurity also seem to more strongly correlate with
presidential vote choice in multiparty provinces than in dominant-party systems (Models 2
and 4). [Table 2, Model 2, Dominant party × Security: -0.005, Standard error = 0.003, p <
.1]”

Replication outcome: Complex test
Inferential criteria: The interaction between the dominant-party system and the
government security evaluation is negative, and statistically significant at the 10% level.
Result: The interaction between the dominant-party system and the sociotropic economic
evaluation is negative: -0.012, standard error = 0.005. The effect is statistically
significant at the 5% level (p = 0.014), two-tailed test. Consequently, this claim was
replicated.
decisions.location: Claim evaluations (contiguous failure and success comparisons)
decisions.reason: The replication report evaluates five preregistered claims from Hiskey and Moseley (2018): three claims concerning sociotropic economic evaluations (Traces 1, 4, and 5) were not replicated, whereas two claims concerning government security evaluations (Traces 6 and 7) were replicated, resulting in a mixed outcome for the original paper.
